stem: Which of the following is the critical initial event ('Hit 1') in the multi-hit pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy?

options.text: Production of galactose-deficient IgA1 (Gd-IgA1) in mucosal lymphoid tissue
Formation of IgG autoantibodies against glomerular basement membrane
Overactivation of classical complement pathway by C1q
Direct cytotoxicity of podocytes mediated by anti-PLA2R antibodies

stem: Immunofluorescence microscopy of a kidney biopsy specimen from a patient with IgA nephropathy typically demonstrates which of the following characteristic features?

options.text: Full-house staining positive for IgG, IgM, IgA, C3, and C1q
Dominant mesangial IgA and C3 deposition with negative C1q staining
Linear capillary wall staining for IgG along the glomerular basement membrane
Subepithelial granular deposits containing anti-PLA2R and IgG4

stem: According to the Oxford Classification of IgA nephropathy (MEST-C score), which of the following pathological features is recognized as the STRONGEST independent predictor of eGFR decline and progressive kidney disease?

options.text: M1 (Mesangial hypercellularity in >50% of glomeruli)
E1 (Endocapillary hypercellularity)
T1 or T2 (Tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis)
C1 (Crescents in <25% of glomeruli)

stem: A 28-year-old man with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy presents with stable serum creatinine (1.0 mg/dL). His kidney biopsy shows crescents in 15% of glomeruli (C1 score). According to KDIGO 2021/2025 guidelines, what is the most appropriate management regarding the crescents?

options.text: Immediately initiate high-dose IV pulse methylprednisolone plus cyclophosphamide
Do not start immunosuppressive therapy solely for crescents if renal function is stable; optimize supportive care
Perform emergent plasmapheresis to clear circulating crescents
Start maintenance rituximab therapy for active crescentic glomerulonephritis

stem: A 24-year-old woman with IgA nephropathy presents with full-blown nephrotic syndrome (proteinuria 6.5 g/day, serum albumin 2.2 g/dL). Renal biopsy reveals mild mesangial IgA deposits on IF, but electron microscopy shows diffuse podocyte foot process effacement (>80%). How should this 'Podocytopathic IgAN' variant be managed?

options.text: Treat with high-dose glucocorticoids as per Minimal Change Disease (MCD) protocol
Initiate IV cyclophosphamide and plasma exchange immediately
Avoid glucocorticoids completely and give only SGLT2 inhibitors
Refer for urgent bilateral nephrectomy due to rapid progression

stem: What is the primary target for urinary protein excretion during the initial 3 to 6 months of optimized supportive care in patients with IgA nephropathy?

options.text: < 0.5 to 1.0 g/day
< 3.5 g/day
< 0.05 g/day (completely zero)
< 5.0 g/day

stem: A patient with IgA nephropathy is started on Dapagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor). At week 3, repeat serum creatinine increases from 1.4 mg/dL to 1.6 mg/dL (eGFR dips by 15%). Which of the following statements correctly explains this finding?

options.text: This is an expected hemodynamic eGFR dip caused by tubuloglomerular feedback and afferent arteriolar constriction
This indicates acute tubular necrosis induced by direct SGLT2 inhibitor nephrotoxicity
The SGLT2 inhibitor should be immediately discontinued and high-dose steroids initiated
This reflects acute allergic interstitial nephritis requiring urgent renal biopsy

stem: Sparsentan is a novel therapeutic agent approved for IgA nephropathy. What is its mechanism of action?

options.text: Dual Endothelin Type A (ETA) and Angiotensin II Type 1 (AT1) receptor antagonist
Targeted-release corticosteroid acting on ileal Peyer's patches
Monoclonal antibody against B-cell activating factor (BAFF)
Selective inhibitor of complement Factor B in the alternative pathway

stem: Targeted-release Budesonide (Nefecon / TRF-Budesonide) is uniquely formulated to deliver glucocorticoids to which specific anatomical site in patients with IgA nephropathy?

options.text: Distal ileum targeting Peyer's patches in the mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT)
Proximal convoluted tubule to block megalin-mediated protein reabsorption
Splenic red pulp to destroy autoantibody-producing plasma cells
Hepatic Kupffer cells to enhance IgA immune complex clearance

stem: According to the TESTING trial and KDIGO guidelines, which of the following is a MANDATORY co-prescription when initiating systemic glucocorticoids for IgA nephropathy?

options.text: Prophylaxis for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) such as Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole
High-dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG)
Prophylactic plasmapheresis prior to each steroid dose
Concurrent oral cyclophosphamide for all low-risk patients

stem: In which patient population does KDIGO specifically highlight Mycophenolate Mofetil (MMF) as an effective steroid-sparing immunosuppressive agent for IgA nephropathy?

options.text: Asian patients with persistent proteinuria despite optimized supportive care
Caucasian patients with baseline eGFR < 15 mL/min/1.73m2
Pediatric patients with minimal change disease only
Patients with acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis

stem: Which novel therapeutic category directly targets B-cell survival factors (BAFF/APRIL) to reduce Gd-IgA1 production in IgA nephropathy?

options.text: Dual BAFF/APRIL inhibitors (such as Sibeprenlimab or Telitacicept)
SGLT2 inhibitors (such as Empagliflozin)
Calcimimetic agents (such as Cinacalcet)
Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (such as Finerenone)

stem: Secondary IgA nephropathy is commonly observed in patients with advanced alcoholic liver cirrhosis. What is the underlying pathophysiology?

options.text: Impaired clearance of circulating IgA immune complexes by hepatic Kupffer cells
Overproduction of IgA autoantibodies driven by hepatitis B viral surface antigen
Direct cytotoxic effect of ethanol on glomerular mesangial cells
Depletion of hepatic complement C3 causing systemic complement activation

stem: A 10-year-old boy presents with palpable purpura on his buttocks and lower extremities, colicky abdominal pain, and microscopic hematuria. A kidney biopsy shows mesangial proliferative GN with dominant IgA deposits on IF. Which statement correctly distinguishes IgA Vasculitis (HSP) from Primary IgA Nephropathy?

options.text: Renal histopathology on biopsy is identical; differentiation relies on systemic extrarenal manifestations
IgA Vasculitis strictly lacks C3 deposition on immunofluorescence
Primary IgA Nephropathy manifests with lower extremity purpura while IgA Vasculitis does not
Electron microscopy shows humps in IgA Vasculitis but line deposits in IgAN

stem: Which of the following gastrointestinal conditions is strongly associated with secondary IgA nephropathy due to mucosal barrier breakdown and increased antigen exposure?

options.text: Celiac disease (gluten-sensitive enteropathy)
Helicobacter pylori gastritis
Clostridioides difficile colitis
Agalactasia enteritis

stem: Which immunosuppressive drug used in solid organ transplantation has been reported to induce de novo IgA nephropathy or FSGS?

options.text: Sirolimus (mTOR inhibitor)
Tacrolimus (calcineurin inhibitor)
Mycophenolate mofetil
Basiliximab (IL-2R antagonist)

stem: A 35-year-old man presents with a generalized maculopapular rash, palmoplantar lesions, microscopic hematuria, and proteinuria (1.8 g/day). Serology reveals positive VDRL and RPR. Kidney biopsy shows IgA deposition. Which infectious disease is responsible for this secondary IgAN/membranous presentation?

options.text: Secondary Syphilis (Treponema pallidum infection)
Primary HIV acute seroconversion
Epstein-Barr virus mononucleosis
Acute Hepatitis A infection

stem: In patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) secondary to IgA nephropathy who receive a kidney transplant, what is the reported rate of IgAN recurrence in the renal allograft?

options.text: 20% to 60% over long-term follow-up, though graft loss occurs in a minority
0% (IgAN never recurs post-transplant)
100% within the first week post-transplant leading to hyperacute rejection
Strictly limited to living donor transplants only
